article_title: Training the next generation of computational scientists through a new undergraduate course
citation: Tulin Kaman, Rouben Rostamian and Shannon W. Dingman. (2022). Training the next generation of computational scientists through a new undergraduate course. https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.01488
title: XSEDE-EMPOWER three-tier undergraduate research participation ladder: learner, apprentice, intern
description: The XSEDE-EMPOWER program, run under the National Computational Science Institute with Shodor support, creates funded undergraduate research positions in faculty mentors' research groups. It organizes participation into three tiers by skill level: "learner, apprentice, and intern". A learner with no scientific computing experience builds skills through online tutorials, workshops, and self-learning; an apprentice begins transforming knowledge into skills with additional training in debugging and performance tools; after completing these two levels in two semesters, students are accepted as interns.
requirements: A faculty mentor submitting a research proposal; stipend support per quarter, semester, summer, or longer
constraints: Progression through learner and apprentice levels takes two semesters before intern status
target_learners: undergraduate students from any U.S. degree-granting institution, from no computing experience upward
examples: A 2019 XSEDE learner (Drinh) was later accepted to the University of Missouri-Kansas City, and a 2021 apprentice-and-intern (De-La Cruz) intends to pursue a Ph.D. in CSE
key_sources: Tulin Kaman, Rouben Rostamian and Shannon W. Dingman. (2022). Training the next generation of computational scientists through a new undergraduate course. https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.01488
